newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese judges clear release of Iraqi diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese judges clear release of Iraqi diplomats.

text.p: A Lebanese judicial committee on Thursday cleared the way for the release on bail of three Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the 1994 murder of Iraqi dissident Taleb as-Suheil in Beirut.
The three diplomats, who were expected to be freed from Roumyeh jail later on Thursday, have been held without trial since their arrest immediately after Suheil's April 12, 1994 murder.

The three-judge committee rejected an appeal by Suheil's widow against a magistrate's decision on Monday to free diplomats Mohammad Kazem, Ali Darwish and Hadi Hassan on a bail of 50,000 Lebanese pounds ($32) each.

The committee also affirmed the magistrate's decision to free a Lebanese suspect, shopowner George Tarjanian, on bail of 300,000 pounds ($194). Suheil's widow has also appealed against the release of Tarjanian, who is accused of links to the murder.
Baghdad and Beirut swiftly broke diplomatic ties after the murder of Suheil, an opponent of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, and arrest of the diplomats.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Wednesday that under international law his country could not put the Iraqi diplomats on trial but could kick them out.

Lebanese authorities said in 1995 they were waiting for the foreign ministry to say whether the suspects were diplomats or non-diplomatic staff. Judicial sources said on Monday the ministry confirmed their diplomatic status last week but gave no explanation for the delay.
A fourth diplomat, commercial attache Khaled Khalaf who was also arrested in connection with the murder, died in custody of a brain haemorrhage in June 1995.
